#### **8) 2 Embodied AI Beginner’s Guide**

- Open-source content: https://github.com/datawhalechina/every-embodied
- Learning guide knowledge base: [ Learning Guide ](https://datawhale-eai.feishu.cn/wiki/QvxQwV2Qyij1NakV9IdcjTl1nJd)
- Q&A section: [ Issue records and summaries ](https://datawhale-eai.feishu.cn/wiki/DBSpwQysHiO9MbkA24qc4Xrxndd)
- The teaching assistant should apply for editing rights to this document. All contents such as check-in information and excellent assignments should be summarized in: [ 1st group, 202603 ](https://datawhale-eai.feishu.cn/wiki/UHAjw8VEjivkbRkBrI7cGZCJnFE) and [ 2nd group, 202603 ](https://datawhale-eai.feishu.cn/wiki/DgZDwGlgyifTwLkcfSpcbZJlndb)
- Course description:

Embodied AI is very trendy. From Mobile ALOHA to Pi0 and OpenVLA, SOTA models are updated almost every week. However, many people want to get involved but get stuck at the first step:

🤯 The materials are too fragmented; not sure where to start learning from?

🤯 The threshold is too high; the mathematical derivations and physics engine are exhausting?

🤯 Can't run, and the environment configuration is so complicated that it makes you doubt everything?

Don’t panic! This beginner-friendly tutorial, Every-Embodied: Zero to Hero, initiated by Datawhale and refined by the open-source community, is now officially open source!🌟 Our focus is on: easy for beginners, reproducible in engineering, and adaptable to cutting-edge technologies. It takes you from a single line of Python code to gradually installing a “brain” for the robot!🧠

Reject the “environment setup from basics to abandonment” approach! We provide ready-to-use environment scripts. Even with only basic programming skills, just three command steps are enough to run the first MuJoCo robotic arm grasping demo locally. We will help you get OpenVLA, SmolVLA, ETPNav working, and even replicate the martial arts robot featured at the Spring Festival Gala! Additionally, 🎬 there are beginner-friendly video tutorials! We have updated numerous practical videos on REDnote and B 站 simultaneously! From Mujoco simulation, ACT grasping water cup algorithms to GenieSim one-click startup, we will guide you step by step to avoid common pitfalls.

​

- Target audience: Students, engineers, and researchers interested in embodied AI; those with a foundation in Python and basic mathematical knowledge. Beginners in Python / AI developers: Those who want to systematically transition into embodied AI fields; university students: Those needing course projects or final projects, or those aiming to quickly develop the ability to reproduce research results; hardware/robotics enthusiasts: Those seeking to establish a complete closed loop from physical machine control to Sim2Real deployment.
- Course ID: 929
- Number of learning groups: 2
- Number of participants per group: 180
